\texttt{schema} & const & c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}1 & yes & -- & The document schema identifier, chancadem.hp500.comparison/v1. \\
\texttt{source} & object & -- & yes & -- & The source publication of the surveys (Rocha, Campos, Silva and Tavares 2024), as the survey reader states it. \\
\texttt{source.\allowbreak{}paper} & string & -- & yes & -- & Authors, year and title of the source publication. \\
\texttt{source.\allowbreak{}doi} & const & 1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}9 & yes & -- & The DOI of the source publication. \\
\texttt{source.\allowbreak{}license} & const & C\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0 & yes & -- & The licence of the source data, which the derived document carries. \\
\texttt{source.\allowbreak{}table} & string & -- & yes & -- & The table of the source publication the survey rows are transcribed from. \\
\texttt{engine\_\allowbreak{}version} & string & pattern \textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{}\$ & yes & -- & The product version that wrote the document (format X.XX.XXX); a version other than VERSION makes the row stale. \\
\texttt{n} & integer & >= 3 & yes & -- & The number of surveys paired (ten in the committed build); every per-survey list has this length. \\
\texttt{bootstrap} & object & -- & yes & -- & How the paired intervals are resampled: the resampling of the CrusherBayes manuscript. \\
\texttt{bootstrap.\allowbreak{}method} & string & -- & yes & -- & The resampling in words: a percentile bootstrap over the surveys of the mean paired difference. \\
\texttt{bootstrap.\allowbreak{}resamples} & integer & >= 1 & yes & -- & The number B of bootstrap resamples of the survey indices (20,000 in the committed build). \\
\texttt{bootstrap.\allowbreak{}seed} & integer & -- & yes & -- & The seed of numpy.random.default\_rng that draws the resampled survey indices (42). \\
\texttt{bootstrap.\allowbreak{}quantiles} & array of number & exactly 2 items & yes & \% & The lower and upper percentiles of the 95 percent interval, 2.5 and 97.5. \\
\texttt{inputs} & object & -- & yes & -- & The two documents the comparison is computed from, with their schema and product version. \\
\texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}loo} & object & -- & yes & -- & The CrusherCal held-out document (hp500-loo) the predictions are read from. \\
\texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}loo.\allowbreak{}path} & string & -- & yes & -- & The input's path relative to data/derived. \\
\texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}loo.\allowbreak{}schema} & string & -- & yes & -- & The schema identifier the input document declares. \\
\texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}loo.\allowbreak{}engine\_\allowbreak{}version} & string & pattern \textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{}\$ & yes & -- & The product version that wrote the input document. \\
\texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}crusherbayes} & object or null & -- & yes & -- & The CrusherBayes document (hp500-crusherbayes) when it is in the build; null when it is absent. Its fields are those of \texttt{inputs.\allowbreak{}loo}. \\
\texttt{crusherbayes} & object & -- & yes & -- & Whether CrusherBayes takes part in the comparison. \\
\texttt{crusherbayes.\allowbreak{}included} & boolean & -- & yes & -- & True when the CrusherBayes document is present and sampled on the same surveys, so its rows are paired. \\
\texttt{crusherbayes.\allowbreak{}note} & object or null & -- & yes & -- & Why CrusherBayes is not compared (its document is absent or was sampled on other surveys); null when it is included. \\
\texttt{crusherbayes.\allowbreak{}note.\allowbreak{}en} & string & -- & yes & -- & The English text. \\
\texttt{crusherbayes.\allowbreak{}note.\allowbreak{}es} & string & -- & yes & -- & The Spanish text. \\
\texttt{targets} & object & -- & yes & -- & The comparison per measured target: throughput (tph) and power (kW). \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph} & object & -- & yes & -- & The comparison on the measured throughput, errors in percent of the measured t/h. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}measured} & array of number & at least 3 items & yes & t/h or kW & The measured values of the target at each survey, in survey order. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}methods} & array of object & at least 2 items & yes & -- & Every method with its MAPE and its per-survey errors, in the order the App lists them. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}methods[].\allowbreak{}id} & string & -- & yes & -- & The method's key as its source document stores it: a key of the strict block of hp500-loo, or crusherbayes. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}methods[].\allowbreak{}control} & boolean & -- & yes & -- & True for a control (the constant mean and the label shuffle), which is never recommended. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}methods[].\allowbreak{}mape\_\allowbreak{}pct} & number & >= 0 & yes & \% & The method's held-out MAPE as its source document states it. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}methods[].\allowbreak{}ape\_\allowbreak{}pct} & array of number or null & at least 3 items & yes & \% & The held-out absolute percentage error at each survey, in survey order; null for the label shuffle, whose per-survey predictions no document stores. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}recommended} & string & -- & yes & -- & The method with the lowest MAPE among the methods that are not controls (a tie keeps the listing order). \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}runner\_\allowbreak{}up} & string & -- & yes & -- & The method with the next lowest MAPE among the methods that are not controls. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired} & array of object & -- & yes & -- & One paired row per method with per-survey predictions, other than the recommended one. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}method} & string & -- & yes & -- & The method compared. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}against} & string & -- & yes & -- & The method it is compared against: always the recommended method of the target. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}mean\_\allowbreak{}diff\_\allowbreak{}pts} & number & -- & yes & points & The mean over the surveys of d\_i = APE\_i(method) - APE\_i(recommended); positive when the method is worse. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}ci95} & array of number & exactly 2 items & yes & points & The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the mean of d over the bootstrap resamples: the 95 percent interval. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}wins} & integer & >= 0 & yes & -- & The number of surveys on which the recommended method has the strictly lower absolute percentage error. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph.\allowbreak{}paired[].\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}better} & number & >= 0; <= 1 & yes & fraction & The share of resamples whose mean of d is above zero: how often the recommended method is better on average. \\
\texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}kW} & object & -- & yes & -- & The comparison on the measured power, errors in percent of the measured kW. Its fields are those of \texttt{targets.\allowbreak{}tph}. \\
